newsitem.title: USA: Clinton wants Shapiro in Commerce slot - report.
newsitem.headline: Clinton wants Shapiro in Commerce slot - report.

text.p: Robert Shapiro, a leading advocate of fiscal restraint and free trade as Democratic Party policies, is President Clinton's choice for a senior Commerce Department job, the Washington Post reported Tuesday.
Clinton plans to nominate Shapiro, a key adviser in his 1992 campaign, as undersecretary for economic affairs, the paper said, citing unnamed administation sources.
If confirmed by the Senate, Shapiro would oversee, among other tasks, the census that takes place every 10 years.

Shapiro is a founder and vice president of the Progressive Policy Institute, a think tank affiliated with the Democratic Leadership Council. Clinton has had a somewhat turbulent relationship with the council, a group he chaired before running for president.
"The choice (of Shapiro) reflects the close ties the president is keeping in his second term with the centrist Democratic Leadership Council," the Post reported.
